title: A Detention for the Locker
premise: Mirabel Fairweather, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, has survived three years by being unremarkable — until a scheduling error pairs him with his tormentor, Julian Voss, for the semester-long Legacy Project. Digging into the school's archives for their assignment, they uncover that Ashgrove's beloved founder built his fortune on stolen patents, including one belonging to Mirabel's late grandfather, and that the administration has been quietly erasing the evidence. When Mirabel threatens to go public, the headmaster retaliates by revoking his scholarship days before finals. With Julian unexpectedly switching sides, Mirabel must expose the truth at the academy's championship assembly — winning neither the trophy nor the argument, but something rarer: a place where he actually belongs.
about_author: Casper Kavanagh is a former boarding-school scholarship kid who spent more afternoons in detention than he admits to. He writes stories about outsiders who discover that fitting in was never the point.

chapters.title: The Scheduling Error
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. On the first day of senior year, Mirabel learns he's been paired with Julian Voss — the boy who made middle school unbearable — for the Legacy Project, and refusing means losing his scholarship. Their first archive session is hostile and silent until Mirabel notices a patent document with his grandfather's name on it, misfiled among the founder's papers. The beat: dread curdling into a dangerous flicker of curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel, alternating with Julian's journal entries. The pair digs deeper and finds a pattern of erased names — inventors whose work the founder claimed — and realizes someone in the administration is still shredding records today. Julian, shaken, stops sabotaging the project; an uneasy truce forms over late nights in the stacks. The beat: two enemies discovering they're investigating the same crime from opposite sides.

chapters.title: Revoked
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. When Mirabel confronts Headmaster Crane privately, Crane offers him silence in exchange for keeping his scholarship — then revokes it anyway when word leaks through Julian's careless text. Ostracized, Mirabel nearly quits, but Julian publicly takes the blame at the winter assembly, splitting the school into factions. The beat: betrayal, then the shocking warmth of an ally standing alone beside him.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. At the spring championship assembly, instead of presenting the safe project, Mirabel and Julian project the recovered patents onto the auditorium screen before the trustees and press. Crane resigns; the stolen legacy is acknowledged, and an endowed scholarship is created in Mirabel's grandfather's name. Mirabel loses the academic prize but gains a community that finally sees him. The beat: quiet triumph — justice won outside the rules, belonging earned inside them.
